trajectory_summary: This call opens easy and stays procedurally on-track, with the rep completing verify cleanly and booking a specific day and time. Energy dips mid-call during the bill-navigation struggle and the utility billing-error disclosure, but the rep's patience recovers it and the call ends calm and agreed. The main gap is missed emotional leverage — a live $584/$1,039 bill shock was captured as data but never flipped into urgency.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (9AM) were mutually agreed and confirmed again at button-up ('We'll give you a call tomorrow at 9AM.'). The wife, identified as a possible co-owner at 02:11, was never explicitly invited onto the appointment call.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I just got a bill for $584.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The bill was captured ($584 / $1,039 back-charge) but the rep only reacted with 'That's a big jump there' at 10:51 instead of tying it to the customer's own 'I would've been shocked' line at 10:53 to anchor urgency for the appointment.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep asked how the customer preferred to send the bill at 05:21; the customer agreed to text photos and then confirmed receipt of the rep's text during the call.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Bill flip missed at peak leverage moment
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I just got a bill for $584.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Customer discovered a shocking, real-time bill number and even labeled it 'shocking' himself at 10:53 — the rep never converted this into urgency for the appointment, the single biggest miss on the call.

key_moments.quote: and a lot of my neighbors have it.
key_moments.stewart_read: Neighbor-influence is a strong social-proof reason to act; rep acknowledged generically but didn't reflect it back as leverage.

key_moments.quote: But, you know, I have a problem with the bill.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep treats this purely as a logistics problem (which months to use) rather than an opening to align against the utility ('sounds like Excel's error cost you money you shouldn't owe').

key_moments.quote: I just got a bill for $584.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the single highest-leverage bill-pain moment in the call and it passes with only 'That's a big jump there.'

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer himself frames the number as shocking, handing the rep the exact emotional cue to flip; rep responds only with logistics ('that'll be perfect to help us... get you a good design started').
